752: 10.4.1 Adjust Outcast.Look at the cards in the Lost Souls pile, ignoring birds. The suit with the most cards becomes the new Outcast—move the outcast marker, showing its Outcast side, to that suit. If that suit was already the Outcast, flip the marker to Hated. If no one suit had the most cards, the marker stays on its current suit and, if it is not Hated, flips to its Hated side.
753: 
754: 10.4.2 Discard Lost Souls.Discard all of the cards in the Lost Souls pile to the discard pile. *(Dominance cards become available to take.)*
755: 
756: 10.4.3 Perform Conspiracies.You can spend acolytes, returning them to your supply, to perform conspiracies in clearings matching the Outcast, in any order and number, as follows. If the Outcast is Hated, the conspiracy costs one fewer acolyte.
757: 
758: **Q:**Can I use Convert or Sanctify to only remove a warrior or building, but not place my own warrior or building there?
759: 
760: **A:**Nope! The rule says that “you must complete the conspiracy,” and faction rules overrule general rules if you cannot fulfill them both.
761: 
762: 1. Crusade.Spend two acolytes to initiate a battle in an Outcast clearing or to move *(at least one warrior)* from an Outcast clearing and then, if you wish, initiate a battle in the destination clearing.
763: 2. Convert.Spend two acolytes to replace an enemy warrior from an Outcast clearing with a Cult warrior. *(To replace a piece, you must be able to remove the old piece and place the new piece.)*
764: 3. Sanctify.Spend three acolytes to replace an enemy building from an Outcast clearing with a garden of the Outcast suit.
765: 
766: 10.5Daylight
767: 
768: You may reveal any number of cards and perform one ritual per card revealed, in any order and number, as follows. *(Reveal cards from your hand into your play area. They cannot be used for any other purposes during Daylight.)*
769: 
770: 10.5.1 Build.In a clearing you rule matching the revealed card, place a garden whose printed suit matches the clearing suit.
771: 
772: 10.5.2 Recruit.In a clearing matching the revealed card, place a warrior.
773: 
774: 10.5.3 Score.Spend the same card you reveal *(placing in Lost Souls)* to score the victory points listed above the rightmost empty Gardens space of the suit matching the revealed card. You cannot Score if no gardens of that suit are on the map. You may perform this only once per turn per suit.
775: 
776: 10.5.4 Sacrifice.Place a warrior in the Acolytes box. To perform this ritual, you must reveal a bird card.
777: 
778: 10.6Evening
779: 
780: Your Evening has three steps in the following order.
781: 
782: 10.6.1 Return Revealed Cards.Return all cards you revealed this turn to your hand.
783: 
784: 10.6.2 Craft.You may craft by activating gardens whose printed suit matches the Outcast suit.
785: 
786: 10.6.3 Draw and Discard.Draw one card, plus one card per uncovered draw bonus. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.

788: 11.Riverfolk Company
789: 
790: 11.1Overview
791: 
792: When news arrived that the Woodland on the shore of the great lake was descending into all-out war, the Riverfolk Company quickly dispatched its officers to set up shop. As other factions purchase their services, the Riverfolk can further entrench their commercial interests by establishing trade posts along the river, scoring victory points. So too can they score points by raw accumulation of funds, but a big treasury makes for an easy target, so the Riverfolk must take care in expanding their operations across the dangerous forest.
793: 
794: 11.2Faction Rules and Abilities
795: 
796: 11.2.1 Crafting.The Riverfolk craft during Daylight by committing funds to empty spaces on the Trade Posts tracks. *(They have no crafting pieces.)*
797: 
798: 11.2.2 Swimmers.The Riverfolk treat rivers as paths and may move along a river fully linking an origin and destination clearing, ignoring the need for rule. *(They can still move using paths.)*
799: 
800: 11.2.3 Public Hand.The Riverfolk place their hand face up above their faction board. *(If a random card is taken from the Riverfolk, the cards are flipped face down, shuffled, drawn from, and then flipped face up.)*
801: 
802: 11.2.4 Funds.To take many actions, the Riverfolk commit and spend funds: warriors in their Funds box.
803: 
804: 11.2.5 Trade Posts.The Riverfolk score victory points when they place trade posts.
805: 
806: 1. Trade Disruption.Whenever a trade post is removed, the Riverfolk remove half of their funds, rounded up, and remove the trade post from the game permanently.
807: 
808: 11.2.6 Buying Services.At the start of another player's Birdsong, that player may buy Riverfolk services.
809: 
810: **Q:**Can I not consent to the action of another player?
811: 
812: **A:**Nope, there are no actions in Root that require consent. For example, the Vagabond does not require consent to form a coalition with someone or Aid someone, and a player does not need the Riverfolk's consent to buy services from them.
813: 
814: **Q:**Can the Riverfolk refuse to sell you one of their services?
815: 
816: **A:**Nope! As long as you pay the cost, you get the service.
817: 
818: 1. Cost.The buyer must place warriors from their supply into the Riverfolk's Payments box equal in number to the cost of that service listed on the Riverfolk's Services track.
819: 2. Number of Services.Each turn, a player may buy one service plus one per clearing with a trade post and their faction pieces.
820: 3. Vagabond Funds.The Vagabond pays for services by exhausting items—for each item he exhausts to do so, the Riverfolk place one Riverfolk warrior in the Payments box.
821: 
822: 11.2.7 Riverfolk Services.The Riverfolk offer three services, as follows.
823: 
824: **Q:**When I hire Riverfolk mercenaries, can I start a battle with them even if I don't have pieces in the clearing where I'm battling?
825: 
826: **A:**Go for it! Plus, if you don't have any warriors there, there's no one to split hits with.
827: 
828: **Q:**Can Riverfolk Mercenaries be used to battle hirelings controlled by the Riverfolk?
829: 
830: **A:**Yes! Mercenaries just won't battle against the Riverfolk themselves, not controlled hirelings.
831: 
832: 1. Hand Card.The buyer takes any card from the Riverfolk's hand and adds it to their hand. *(The buyer may buy this service multiple times as long as they have access to enough trade posts.)*
833: 2. Riverboats.The buyer treats rivers as paths until the end of their turn.
834: 3. Mercenaries.During Daylight and Evening of this turn, except when battling the Riverfolk, the buyer treats Riverfolk warriors as their own for rule and for battle. *(The buyer cannot move them, count them toward dominance, or remove them except by taking hits. They are no longer enemy pieces, but they are still Riverfolk faction pieces, so they cannot be affected by abilities such as the Marquise's Field Hospitals or used in actions such as the Duchy's Sway Ministers.)*
835:    1. Taking Hits.The buyer must split hits, taking odd hits by removing owned *(not Riverfolk)* warriors, if any, or owned buildings or tokens only if they have no warriors *(including Riverfolk)* in the clearing of battle.
836:    2. Vagabond & Mercenaries.The Vagabond cannot buy Riverfolk Mercenaries. If Riverfolk Mercenaries are removed in a battle against the Vagabond, the Vagabond does not become Hostile with the Riverfolk.
837: 
838: 11.3Faction Setup
839: 
840: 11.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors.Form a supply of 15 warriors.
841: 
842: 11.3.2 Step 2: Place Warriors.Place 4 warriors in any clearings touching the river.
843: 
844: 11.3.3 Step 3: Fill Trade Posts Tracks.Place 9 trade posts on the matching spaces of your Trade Posts tracks.
845: 
846: 11.3.4 Step 4: Gain Starting Funds.Place 3 warriors in your Payments box.
847: 
848: 11.3.5 Step 5: Set Starting Prices.Place 1 service marker on any space of each of your Services tracks.
849: 
850: 11.4Birdsong
851: 
852: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.
853: 
854: 11.4.1 Protectionism.If the Payments box is empty, place two warriors in it.
855: 
856: 11.4.2 Score Dividends.If there are any trade posts on the map, score one victory point per two funds. *(Do not score for warriors in Payments or Committed.)*
857: 
858: 11.4.3 Gather Funds.Move all warriors on your faction board to the Funds box.
859: 
860: 11.5Daylight
861: 
862: You can commit and spend funds to take actions, as follows, in any order and number. When you commit a fund, move the warrior to the Committed box. When you spend a fund, return the warrior to its owner's supply.
863: 
864: 11.5.1 Move.Commit one fund to take a move.
865: 
866: 11.5.2 Battle.Commit one fund to initiate a battle.
867: 
868: 11.5.3 Craft.Commit funds to craft a card from your hand. Instead of moving these warriors to the Committed box, you must place them on empty spaces of the Trade Posts tracks matching the suits listed on the crafting cost.
869: 
870: **Q:**Can I export a card if the item on it is not in the supply or if I already have its permanent effect?
871: 
872: **A:**Nope! You must be able to craft the card in the first place in order to export it. In these cases, you could not export the card.
873: 
874: 1. Export.You may ignore the listed benefit of crafting a card, discarding it, to place one Riverfolk warrior in the Payments box.
875: 
876: 11.5.4 Draw.Commit one fund to draw a card.
877: 
878: 11.5.5 Recruit.Spend one fund to place a warrior in any clearing with a river.
879: 
880: 11.5.6 Establish Trade Post with Garrison.Spend two funds to place a trade post and a warrior.
881: 
882: 1. Choose Clearing.Choose any clearing without a trade post that is ruled by any player.
883: 2. Spend Funds.Spend two funds of the player who rules the chosen clearing.
884: 3. Place and Score.Place the matching trade post and one warrior in the chosen clearing. Score the victory points listed on the space uncovered on your faction board.
885: 
886: 11.6Evening
887: 
888: Your Evening has two steps in the following order.
889: 
890: 11.6.1 Discard Cards.If you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until there are five.
891: 
892: 11.6.2 Set Costs.You may move each service marker to any space on its track, setting it to a new cost.

894: 12.Underground Duchy
895: 
896: 12.1Overview
897: 
898: The Underground Duchy wants to show the foreign creatures of the Woodland that they would be better off as subjects. As they set up frontier outposts to show their power in the Woodland, the Duchy can sway ministers to the cause, scoring victory points and diverting more of the Duchy's resources. But be careful—a reversal of fortune could spell public humiliation, leading ministers to abandon the task.
899: 
900: 12.2Faction Rules and Abilities
901: 
902: 12.2.1 Crafting.The Duchy crafts during Evening by activating citadels and markets.
903: 
904: 12.2.2 The Burrow.The Burrow is an unsuited clearing adjacent to each clearing with a tunnel token. Non-Duchy pieces cannot be placed in or moved into the Burrow. The Duchy always rules the Burrow *(even with no pieces there)*.
905: 
906: 12.2.3 The Price of Failure.Whenever any number of Duchy buildings are removed, the Duchy returns their swayed minister card of highest rank *(lord, then noble, then squire)* to their Unswayed Ministers pile, and removes its crown from the game permanently, then discards a random card. If they have multiple swayed ministers of highest rank, the Duchy chooses which to return.
907: 
908: 12.2.4 Tunnels.The Duchy has three tunnel tokens. If the Duchy is prompted to place a tunnel but all three tunnels are on the map, the Duchy may first remove any tunnel from the map.
909: 
910: 12.3Faction Setup
911: 
912: 12.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors and Tunnels.Form supplies of 20 warriors and 3 tunnel tokens.
913: 
914: 12.3.2 Step 2: Prepare the Burrow.Place the Burrow board near the map.
915: 
916: 12.3.3 Step 3: Surface.Place 2 warriors and 1 tunnel in a corner clearing that is not the starting corner clearing of another player and, if possible, is diagonally opposite from a starting corner clearing. This is your starting clearing. Then place 2 warriors in each clearing adjacent to the chosen corner clearing, except the Burrow. *(This is updated from earlier printings for flexibility.)*
917: 
918: 12.3.4 Step 4: Fill Buildings Tracks.Place 3 citadels and 3 markets on your respective Buildings spaces.
919: 
920: 12.3.5 Step 5: Collect Ministers.Place 9 minister cards face up on your Unswayed Ministers pile.
921: 
922: 12.3.6 Step 6: Fill Crown Spaces.Place 9 crowns on the spaces with victory points on your faction board.
923: 
924: 12.4Birdsong
925: 
926: Place one warrior, plus one warrior per warrior icon showing, in the Burrow.
927: 
928: 12.5Daylight
929: 
930: Your Daylight has three steps in the following order.
931: 
932: 12.5.1 Assembly.You may take up to two actions in any order and number, as follows.
933: 
934: 1. Build.Reveal one card to place a citadel or market in a matching clearing you rule.
935: 2. Recruit.Place one warrior in the Burrow.
936: 3. Move.Take a move.
937: 4. Battle.Initiate a battle.
938: 5. Dig.Spend one card to place a tunnel token in a matching clearing without a tunnel token. Then, move up to four warriors *(at least one)* from the Burrow to that clearing. *(If all three tunnels are on the map, you may remove a tunnel first.)*
939: 
940: 12.5.2 Parliament.You may take the action of each swayed minister once in any order.
941: 
942: 1. Foremole.Reveal any card to place a citadel or market in any clearing *(matching or not)* you rule.
943: 2. Captain.Initiate a battle.
944: 3. Marshal.Take a move.
945: 4. Brigadier.Take up to two moves or initiate up to two battles.
946: 5. Banker.Spend any number of cards *(even one)* of the same suit to score victory points in equal number.
947: 6. Mayor.Take the action of any swayed noble or squire.
948: 7. Duchess of Mud.Score two victory points if all three tunnels are on the map.
949: 8. Baron of Dirt.Score one victory point per market on the map.
950: 9. Earl of Stone.Score one victory point per citadel on the map.
951: 
952: 12.5.3 Sway.You may sway one minister, as follows.
953: 
954: 1. Choose Minister.Choose a minister card in your Unswayed Ministers pile. You must have a crown on your faction board matching the rank *(squire, noble, lord)* of that minister.
955: 2. Reveal Cards.Reveal the number of cards listed on the chosen minister. For each card you wish to reveal, you must have at least one Duchy piece in a clearing matching the suit of that card. Each such clearing allows you to reveal one matching card.
956: 3. Sway Minister and Score.Take the chosen minister card and place it above your faction board. Take a crown of that minister's rank from your faction board and place it on the minister card. Score the victory points listed on the space uncovered on your faction board.
957: 
958: 12.6Evening
959: 
960: Your Evening has three steps in the following order.
961: 
962: 12.6.1 Discard and Return Revealed Cards.Discard any bird cards you revealed this turn, then return all other cards you revealed this turn to your hand.
963: 
964: 12.6.2 Craft.You may craft by activating citadels and markets. *(These are identical for crafting purposes.)*
965: 
966: 12.6.3 Draw and Discard.Draw one card, plus one card per card draw icon showing. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.
967: 
968: 13.Corvid Conspiracy
969: 
970: 13.1Overview
971: 
972: The Corvid Conspiracy seeks to strong-arm the Woodland into submission by completing criminal plots, scoring victory points each time they flip one. The more revealed plots on the map, the more they score. Misdirection is critical—if their plans are too obvious, the Corvids risk exposure. To avoid this, they must recruit carefully and look for any opportunities for subterfuge and extortion.
973: 
974: 13.2Faction Rules and Abilities
975: 
976: 13.2.1 Crafting.The Corvids craft during Birdsong by activating plot tokens *(whether face up or down)*.
977: 
978: 13.2.2 Plot Tokens.The Corvids have eight plot tokens, two of each type.
979: 
980: 1. Token Facing.While in the Corvids' supply, plot tokens are face down *(feather)*. While on the map, a plot token can be face up *(unique icon)* or face down. The Corvids can inspect any facedown plot token at any time.
981: 2. Placement Limits.Each clearing can hold only one plot token.
982: 
983: 13.2.3 Nimble.The Corvids can move regardless of who rules their origin or destination clearing.
984: 
985: 13.2.4 Exposure.Any number of times on their turn, an enemy with faction pieces in a clearing with a facedown plot token may show the Corvids a matching card to guess the type of plot token in that clearing. If incorrect, the Corvids say "no," and the enemy gives that card to the Corvids. If correct, the enemy removes the plot token *(scoring a victory point)*; if this removes a Raid token, it does not place warriors. *(You cannot use Exposure once you have begun the last step of your turn. See 1.4.3.)*
986: 
987: 13.2.5 Embedded Agents.As defender in battle, if the Corvids have a facedown plot token *(even defenseless)* in the clearing of battle, they deal an extra hit.
988: 
989: 13.3Faction Setup
990: 
991: 13.3.1 Step 1: Gather Warriors and Plots.Form supplies of 15 warriors and 8 plot tokens face down.
992: 
993: 13.3.2 Step 2: Scatter.Place 1 warrior in any clearing of each suit *(total of 3)*.
994: 
995: 13.4Birdsong
996: 
997: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.
998: 
999: 13.4.1 Craft.You may activate plot tokens *(whether face up or down)* to craft cards from your hand.
